name: RepoGraph
status_reason: NOT a standalone baseline agent -- confirmed by direct inspection that RepoGraph itself has no independent question-answering entrypoint. The evaluated system is precisely 'Matched ReAct + RepoGraph': MatchedReActAgent with one additional opt-in tool (search_repograph) backed by RepoGraph's own precomputed structural graph. Verified live end-to-end (1 real smoke question, qibo) after finding and fixing 5 real correctness bugs in the officially released code.
role: repository-structural-graph augmentation tool (Track A), NOT a repository-level QA agent
commit_note: Latest commit on main at audit time ('docs: add hf datasets', 2025-04-01). Verified live via clone.
paper: arXiv:2410.14684, 'RepoGraph: Enhancing AI Software Engineering with Repository-level Code Graph' (Ouyang, Yu, Ma, Xiao, Zhang, Jia, Han, Zhang, Yu -- UIUC/Tencent AI Lab), ICLR 2025.
license: Apache License 2.0 (core repograph/ package). The bundled SWE-agent/ fork's own license was not separately confirmed -- treat as unresolved if that subdirectory specifically is ever redistributed.
STANDALONE_VS_TOOL_FINDING: Confirmed via direct source inspection (not assumed from the paper's own framing): the repo ships NO independent 'ask a question, get an answer' entrypoint. It vendors full copies of Agentless and SWE-agent in-tree; in both, RepoGraph is wired in as one more context-injection/action-space addition to an EXISTING agent loop -- the LLM call that produces a final answer lives in Agentless's/SWE-agent's own code, never in repograph/'s own files (construct_graph.py, graph_searcher.py, utils.py contain zero LLM/openai imports). This directly matches the user's own stated concern: RepoGraph must never be presented as a standalone competitor -- only as 'Matched ReAct + RepoGraph'.

what_it_constructs.nodes: individual lines of code, each classified 'def' (a definition) or 'ref' (a reference/invocation elsewhere)
what_it_constructs.edges: 'invoke' (definition -> reference) and 'contain' (definition -> nested members, e.g. class -> its methods)
what_it_constructs.built_with: tree-sitter (+ tree-sitter-languages, grep-ast) for AST-based parsing; a separate ast-based pass (utils.create_structure) builds a parallel per-file structure dict the tag-extraction logic also reads from
what_it_constructs.no_llm_involved: confirmed -- zero LLM calls anywhere in graph construction; the paper's own optional downstream ego-graph summarization (to cut token cost) is a separate, optional, downstream consumer step, not part of construction itself
what_it_constructs.python_only: CONFIRMED, IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMITATION: CodeGraph.find_files() unconditionally filters to files ending in '.py' -- RepoGraph as released cannot see ANY non-Python source file in a repository, regardless of that repo's actual primary language. Directly relevant to RepoProbe applicability (see third_party/manifests -- RepoProbe includes Swift/C#/Lua/Ruby/PHP/etc. repos RepoGraph would be a pure no-op tool for).

query_api: Navigation-only, no semantic/embedding search: repograph/graph_searcher.py's RepoSearcher exposes one_hop_neighbors/two_hop_neighbors/dfs/bfs (successors only, via networkx). The REAL production query shape used by both the paper's own SWE-agent integration and this suite's own tool is: query by exact function/class NAME, return its immediate predecessors (callers) + successors (callees) + itself -- read directly from the constructed networkx graph's own predecessors()/successors(), not through RepoSearcher (which has no predecessors-equivalent at all).
gpt_4_1_substitution: N/A at the RepoGraph level -- it has no model to substitute (no LLM dependency of its own). The wrapping agent (Matched ReAct) already defaults to gpt-4.1.
porting_effort_to_sweqa_pro_or_repoprobe: SWE-QA-Pro: straightforward for Python repos (all 26 SWE-QA-Pro repos have substantial Python content) -- verified live against qibo. RepoProbe: LIMITED -- only meaningful for RepoProbe's Python-primary-language repos (8/50 per this suite's own earlier RepoProbe audit); a pure no-op tool (search_repograph always returns 'not found') for the other 42. See RepoProbe compatibility matrix in docs/evaluation_plan.md.
integration_design: ant.agents.matched_react.MatchedReActAgent gained a new, OPT-IN, off-by-default constructor parameter (extra_tools: dict[str, Callable[[str, TaskExample], list[Evidence]]], extra_tool_descriptions: dict[str, str]) -- when unset (the default for the plain Matched ReAct baseline), behavior is byte-identical to before this change (confirmed: all 7 existing baseline-invariant tests still pass unmodified). ant.external_wrappers.repograph.RepoGraphTool.as_extra_tool(repo_dir) binds a per-repo query function matching that exact signature. The resulting agent is constructed as MatchedReActAgent(extra_tools={'search_repograph': tool.as_extra_tool(environment_root)}, extra_tool_descriptions={...}) -- this IS the precise 'Matched ReAct + RepoGraph' system: same budget (50), same ANT-parity primitive tool limits, same repo scope (EvalRepoEnvironment), same everything else as plain Matched ReAct, plus exactly one additional tool.
graph_caching: New addition (not in the official release, which always rebuilds from scratch with no cache -- confirmed via direct reading of the __main__ entrypoint): repograph/_ant_query.py caches the constructed graph as a pickle keyed by a hash of the repo's own resolved absolute path, under third_party/checkouts/repograph/_ant_cache/. First construction against qibo (134 eligible .py files): ~10-12s. Cached re-query: near-instant.
environment_strategy: Pinned external checkout under third_party/checkouts/repograph (gitignored, never committed), with its own isolated venv (.venv) -- pip install tree-sitter==0.21.3 tree-sitter-languages==1.10.2 grep-ast==0.3.2 networkx==3.2.1 pygments==2.18.0 tqdm diskcache (the requirements.txt's own openai/tiktoken/libcst entries were NOT installed -- confirmed unused by repograph/'s own core files, only used by the bundled Agentless/SWE-agent integrations this suite does not drive).
execution_status: VERIFIED LIVE (Track A Stage 4): graph construction completes successfully against a real repo (qibo, 134 files) after the 5 fixes below; a real query for 'execute_circuit' returns correct, real results (its own definition location, no false matches). One real end-to-end 'Matched ReAct + RepoGraph' smoke question completed successfully (qibo dev question, agent_declared_finish, 17 llm_calls, $0.066, real evidence returned from search_repograph for 'probabilities'). This is a REDUCED-SCOPE smoke (1 question, not the full 2-4) due to this pass's own session time budget after the substantial debugging effort the 5 bugs below required -- disclosed explicitly, not silently presented as a complete smoke.
local_modifications: get_tags_raw(): rel_fname.split('/') only ever split on the POSIX separator; on Windows, os.path.relpath() (used by this method's own caller) produces backslash-separated paths, so this always produced a single-element list for any file in a subdirectory, raising KeyError on the very next line for every repo with a nested directory structure -- i.e. this crashed on essentially every real repo on Windows. Changed to re.split(r'[\\/]', rel_fname); behavior on POSIX paths (no backslashes) is unchanged.

get_tags_raw(): a 'class'-category tag can be a REFERENCE to a class defined in a DIFFERENT file (tree-sitter's own line-text heuristic, 'class ' in cur_cdl, over-matches), but structure_classes is built from only the CURRENT file's own structure, so tag_name was absent and this raised KeyError on real multi-file repos. The exact fix location had the ORIGINAL AUTHORS' OWN commented-out defensive fallback directly above it (# try: class_functions = self.get_class_functions(...) # except: class_functions = 'None') -- restored as a .get()-based equivalent rather than invented fresh.

get_tags_raw(): same root cause, 'function'-category branch -- structure_all_funcs (built by a SEPARATE, independent AST-based parse in utils.parse_python_file, which disagrees with tree-sitter's own query on some constructs, e.g. property-decorated methods) could be missing tag_name, raising KeyError. Same .get()-based fallback pattern applied.

get_tags_raw(): utils.create_structure() nests a repo-ROOT file (e.g. setup.py) one level under a key equal to the repo directory's own basename, but this lookup never accounted for that -- any file directly in the repo root raised KeyError (i.e. this crashed on essentially every real repo, since most have at least one root-level .py file). Fixed by prepending the repo's own basename to the lookup path when the file has no subdirectory prefix, matching create_structure's own convention exactly.

get_code_graph(): get_tag_files() (via get_ranked_tags/get_tags_raw) yields `Tag` namedtuples (attribute access: tag.name), but tag_to_graph()'s own body uses dict-style bracket access (tag['name']) throughout -- a real internal type-shape mismatch between two parts of this same file, discovered only once graph construction reached the tag-to-graph conversion step (i.e. after processing all 134 files). Fixed by normalizing each Tag namedtuple to a dict (._asdict()) at this one call site, rather than rewriting tag_to_graph's several bracket-access lines.
repograph/_ant_query.py (new file, NOT part of the official release): per-repo graph-caching driver, described in graph_caching above.

Two encoding-related file-read failures were observed but NOT patched (logged-and-skipped by RepoGraph's own existing error handling, not fatal to the overall run): 4/134 qibo files failed to decode under this Windows machine's own default codepage (cp950) rather than UTF-8 -- a real, disclosed, pre-existing non-UTF-8-explicit file-read bug in RepoGraph's own code, left as-is since it degrades gracefully (those 4 files' own tags are simply missing from the graph, not a crash) and fixing it was not necessary to get a working end-to-end result.

repograph/_ant_query.py::_build_or_load_graph: only a successful (non-None) graph is now cached; a None construction result is no longer persisted. Found while diagnosing an unrelated bug in this evaluation suite's OWN diagnostic script (a relative repo_dir path resolved against the wrong cwd, causing a genuine, repeatable None construction result for a nonexistent path) -- once that was traced and fixed on the caller side, this cache behavior was still a real, worth-fixing defensive gap: ANY None construction result, transient or not, was being cached forever, silently returning zero results for every future query against that repo with no error surfaced anywhere. Kept as a genuine hardening fix even though it was not the root cause of the symptom that surfaced it.
known_limitations_not_investigated_furth: Given the number of real bugs already found and fixed to reach a working state, this audit did NOT exhaustively search for every remaining edge case -- it is plausible additional rare per-file failure modes exist in repos not yet tested (only qibo has been exercised end-to-end). Any future use against a new repo should treat a first run as a real test, not assume full reliability from this one repo's success.
vendored_files: None -- no RepoGraph source is vendored into ANT's own tree; all modifications live in the pinned external checkout only.
